content: iOS Safari only allows programmatic .focus() to open the virtual keyboard when called synchronously inside a user-gesture event handler (click, touchend, etc.). AJAX callbacks are asynchronous — they execute outside the original gesture context — so Safari silently ignores .focus() called inside jQuery $.get() or $.post() success callbacks. This is by design, not a bug: Apple's WebKit blocks keyboard popups from async code to prevent unwanted UX. The only reliable workarounds are: (1) do not auto-focus at all, instead scroll the injected element into view; (2) render the form synchronously (not via AJAX), then show/hide it.
